doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sitting in on the neighbor's private kindergarten
summary: A neighbor ran a small school; he sat in with older children and learned numbers and the alphabet very young.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What were some of the things you might hear from the other house?
I don’t know whether I should pursue that any further. Was there music coming from . . .?

Yeah, you could hear just about everything. I recall that. The neighbor was a teacher, like a private school teacher, what we would call now kindergarten classes at a private school. That’s what this woman did for a living. People left their children there – very young kids there, and they were taught there. I used to go over and sit in. I wasn’t one of the – you might call the pupils that was hired – that the people brought over. I was much younger than most of the students that this woman taught, but I’d go over there and sit in class with them. I learned to read pretty young.
Do you remember in terms of what you learned? Was it your numbers? Your alphabet?
I learned numbers very well, and I learned the alphabets, like they were taught: a-b-c-d-e­ f-g-g-h-i-j-k-l-m-n-o-p-q-r-s-t-u-v-w-x-y-z period. And from 1 to 100 and from then on.
